title: Information Recovery by Spline Moment Sieves in Feedback Duration Panels
banked_reason: D0.5.G tier=incremental below field floor; paper_score_ceiling 5.9 < 7.4, with both math and decision referees passing after the marginal-DQM repair.
gap_reasons: The note proves a sharp population Hilbert-space obstruction for deterministic finite FHR spaces and an exact approximation frontier for one sinusoidal feedback family, but it does not prove an efficiency obstruction for any implemented estimator: there is no stochastic dimension schedule, sampling theorem, asymptotic distribution, or feasible variance result.

The exact constants and identification certificates make the result worthwhile, but the absence of estimator-level consequences and practical evidence keeps it below a field-level econometrics contribution and constrains the projected paper score. [D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 5.9 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'subfield' is capped at 'incremental'.]
proof_attempt_summary: The run proved the deterministic population-oracle obstruction, the named centered-cubic-spline compact-score frontier, and the exact 17/128, 7/64, and 192/119 constants. A rejected fiberwise observed-law DQM argument was replaced by a parameter-independent Markov-kernel contraction theorem; the rerun then passed both math and decision review with no findings. The package remained below the field floor because an estimator-level theorem would require a new stochastic architecture, not a bounded repair of this result.
tldr: For a standard deterministic centered cubic tensor-product FHR spline implementation, what primitive feedback-complexity boundary separates uniform recovery of semiparametric beta information from fixed loss? The proposal gives an exact frontier in the Gamma-frailty two-spell MPH witness: a common frequency, equivalently Lipschitz, bound makes the score family compact and the nested splines uniformly information-complete, whereas removing that bound permits smooth uniformly positive feedback that forces the same spline oracle to \(7/64\) information while full information tends to \(17/128\), with variance regret \(192/119\) and pilot determinant at least \(1/144\). The architecture-free diagonal theorem is retained; random, adaptive, and all-estimator impossibility remain excluded.
gap: FHR theory identifies the complete robust moment space and full score, and growing-moment econometrics proves positive pointwise results under approximation and sample-size conditions. Neither gives a primitive two-sided complexity boundary for a concrete FHR spline implementation in a feedback duration panel.
fill: Define the off-parameter MPH transforms and regular FHR extensions, verify DQM and the recomputed pilot Jacobian/global roots, prove spline validity and density, establish bounded-frequency uniform recovery by compactness, and pair it with weak escape and exact constants \(17/128,7/64,192/119,1/144\).
